text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 2: For wind power, 53 of 94 product-and-lead rows have a higher error than the ENS mean, 13 have a lower error, and 28 cannot be told apart'
text.tspan: Figure 2: For wind power, 53 of 94 product-and-lead rows have a higher
error than the ENS mean, 13 have a lower error, and 28 cannot be told

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each row is an XGBoost model given one product's weather for the three wind farms. Dot: the product's error minus the ENS mean's at the same lead day, in percentage points of capacity; negative means the product forecasts better. Zero is the ENS mean. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months and a fitting seed. Each row is scored on the hours its product and its ENS mean share. Day 0 is not a lead a live service could use, and it favours the Previous Runs products: they read the freshest run, a lead of a few hours, while ENS reads the 00 UTC run of the day, a lead of 0 to 23 hours. Every error is a fraction of the generator's own capacity, taken as its 99th percentile of metered output. For AIFS Single, AIFS ENS mean, and WeatherNext 3, zero is an ENS mean refitted on their own rows (16, 11, and 7 months). Every other product is compared with the leaderboard's 21-month ENS mean. WeatherNext 3's reference is the ENS mean built from the mean-vector speed, as WeatherNext 3's own speed is. All rows are exploratory.'
text.tspan: Each row is an XGBoost model given one product's weather for the three wind farms. Dot: the product's error minus
the ENS mean's at the same lead day, in percentage points of capacity; negative means the product forecasts better.
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months and a fitting seed.
Each row is scored on the hours its product and its ENS mean share. Day 0 is not a lead a live service could use,
and it favours the Previous Runs products: they read the freshest run, a lead of a few hours, while ENS reads the
00 UTC run of the day, a lead of 0 to 23 hours.
Every error is a fraction of the generator's own capacity, taken as its 99th percentile of metered output.
For AIFS Single, AIFS ENS mean, and WeatherNext 3, zero is an ENS mean refitted on their own rows (16, 11, and 7
months). Every other product is compared with the leaderboard's 21-month ENS mean.
WeatherNext 3's reference is the ENS mean built from the mean-vector speed, as WeatherNext 3's own speed is.
